name: Radius Wallet Convention Consistency
query: Show me how to set up wallets for a fresh Radius testnet agent demo, a Foundry CLI deployment, a viem app script, and one x402 terminal payment.
context: The user needs guidance that crosses Radius skills. The answer must choose the right wallet shape for each workflow without leaking keys: the radius-dev bootstrap helper for fresh agent-created testnet wallets, Foundry keystore accounts for existing terminal wallets, environment-backed private keys for app code, and no raw private keys passed as command-line arguments.
expected_behavior: States the shared Radius wallet convention instead of creating x402-specific or faucet-specific wallet rules
For fresh agent-created testnet wallets: uses radius-wallet-bootstrap.mjs and loads .radius/wallets/<name>.env
For existing CLI, Foundry, cast, forge, and one-off x402 terminal workflows: instructs the user to create a named keystore with cast wallet import <name> --interactive
For existing CLI keystore workflows: uses --account <name> or --account "$CAST_ACCOUNT" for signing and transactions
For existing CLI keystore workflows: sets CAST_ACCOUNT=<name> and derives OWNER with cast wallet address --account "$CAST_ACCOUNT"
For app-code and viem examples: loads PRIVATE_KEY or RADIUS_PRIVATE_KEY from environment variables
For faucet/address-only cases: distinguishes address ownership from signing access and stops if a signed flow is required but no key material or keystore is available
Warns never to log, hardcode, display, or commit private keys
success_criteria: Includes radius-wallet-bootstrap.mjs for fresh agent-created testnet wallets
Includes cast wallet import <name> --interactive or an equivalent named-account import command for existing CLI wallets
Includes --account <name> or --account "$CAST_ACCOUNT" for CLI signing or sending
Includes CAST_ACCOUNT for existing CLI keystore workflows
Derives OWNER or the payer address from the Foundry keystore account when possible
Allows PRIVATE_KEY or RADIUS_PRIVATE_KEY only as an environment variable in app-code examples
Does not use CAST_ACCOUNT as the fresh testnet wallet bootstrap path
Does not use --private-key as an executable CLI argument
Does not hardcode a raw private key
Does not print, log, or ask the user to paste private keys into chat
